quotes.text:
linux64-clang-22:
    description: "Clang 22 toolchain build"
    attributes:
        local-toolchain: true
    treeherder:
        symbol: TL(clang-22)
    worker:
        max-run-time: 600
    run:
        script: repack-clang.sh
        toolchain-alias:
            by-project:
                toolchains: null
                default: linux64-clang
        toolchain-artifact: public/build/clang.tar.zst
    fetches:
        toolchain:
            - linux64-cctools-port
            - linux64-clang-22-raw
            - linux64-aarch64-compiler-rt-22

win64-clang-22:
    description: "Clang-cl 22 toolchain build"
    attributes:
        local-toolchain: true
    treeherder:
        symbol: TW64(clang-22)
    worker:
        max-run-time: 600
    run:
        script: repack-clang.sh
        toolchain-alias:
            by-project:
                toolchains: null
                default:
                    - win64-clang
                    - win64-clang-toolchain
        toolchain-artifact: public/build/clang.tar.zst
    fetches:
        toolchain:
            - linux64-cctools-port
            - win64-clang-22-raw
            - linux64-aarch64-compiler-rt-22
            - linux64-x64-compiler-rt-22

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The corrected 1384 Linux and Windows tasks fetch their matching raw compiler labels and matching-version compiler runtimes, while stable aliases remain linux64-clang and win64-clang. At the accepted revision the same structure names version 22, so clang 19 is historical. In this Taskcluster family, recommend checking the platform/version in dependencies as well as the alias used by consumers; a version rename alone can leave a wrong-platform source. This is scoped infrastructure naming guidance, not proof of a built compiler. No test, build or runtime operation was run. Full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion is pending; source landing alone does not establish reviewer approval.
title: Toolchain labels encode platform and version independently of stable aliases
